key_insight: LiftGCN preserves high-frequency stress information on finite-element graphs by lifting the spectrum onto the unit circle with a Joukowski-based recurrence instead of using smoothing message passing.
engineering_relevance: This makes graph-based stress surrogates more reliable for capturing localized peaks near holes, notches, and load points while keeping propagation computationally efficient.
method: Maps the normalized graph operator spectrum to the unit circle via the Joukowski relation.
Uses a simple second-order recurrence with unit-modulus characteristic roots for energy-preserving propagation.
Adds lightweight local nonlinear residuals while requiring only one sparse neighborhood aggregation per layer.
evidence_signal: On finite element stress prediction tasks, the method reports competitive overall accuracy and better reconstruction of stress concentrations and high-gradient structures with lower computational cost.
watch_item: The approach depends on stable normalization and recurrence implementation, so numerical robustness and tuning may matter on large or noisy meshes.
paper_title: LiftGCN: Efficient Energy-Preserving Graph Learning via Joukowski Spectral Lifting for Finite Element Stress Prediction
